passages.text: Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews, especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.
passages.sermon:
King Agrippa spoke to Paul.
He said, “You have permission to speak for yourself.”
Paul stretched out his hand.
He began his defense.
He said, “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today.”
I am defending myself against all the accusations of the Jews.
You know all the Jewish customs and controversies.
Because of this, I am especially glad to speak before you.
I ask you to listen to me patiently.
passages.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ἔφη Ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ὑπὲρ σεαυτοῦ λέγειν Τότε ὁ Παῦλος ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπελογεῖτο Περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα ἥγημαι ἐμαυτὸν μακάριον ἐπὶ σοῦ μέλλων σήμερον ἀπολογεῖσθαι μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε πάντων τῶν κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ἐθῶν τε καὶ ζητημάτων διὸ δέομαι μακροθύμως ἀκοῦσαί μου

passages.text: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from the earliest days of my youth, among my own people and in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
All the Jews know how I have lived.
They know about my life from the earliest days of my youth.
I lived among my own people.
I also lived in Jerusalem.
passages.original: Τὴν μὲν οὖν βίωσίν μου τὴν ἐκ νεότητος τὴν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς γενομένην ἐν τῷ ἔθνει μου ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις ἴσασι πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι

passages.text: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.
passages.sermon:
The Jews have known me for a long time.
They can testify about me if they want to.
I lived as a Pharisee.
The Pharisees follow the strictest group in our religion.
passages.original: προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος

passages.text: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers, the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to realize as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O king, that I am accused by the Jews.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
\r\nPaul is a Jew.
\r\nPaul stands on trial now.
\r\nPaul stands on trial because he hopes in a promise.
\r\nGod made this promise to the fathers of the Jewish people.
\r\nThe twelve tribes of Israel serve God with great effort.
\r\nThey serve God day and night.
\r\nThe twelve tribes hope to receive this promise from God.
\r\nPaul is accused by the Jews because of this hope.
\r\nPaul addresses the king directly.
passages.original: Καὶ νῦν ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τῆς εἰς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἕστηκα κρινόμενος εἰς ἣν τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ἡμῶν ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν λατρεῦον ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι περὶ ἧς ἐλπίδος ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων βασιλεῦ

passages.text: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to King Agrippa and other listeners.
\r\nPaul believes in God.
\r\nPaul knows that God made promises to their ancestors.
\r\nPaul stands on trial because of his hope in God’s promise.
\r\nPaul asks a question.
\r\nPaul says, “Why do you think it is unbelievable if God raises the dead?”
\r\nGod has the power to raise the dead.
\r\nPaul challenges them to consider this truth.
passages.original: τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρ’ ὑμῖν εἰ ὁ Θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει

passages.text: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
I once believed something strongly.
I believed I must act against Jesus of Nazareth.
I thought I should do many things to oppose his name.
passages.original: Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι

passages.text: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.
passages.sermon:
I acted in Jerusalem.
I had authority from the chief priests.
I put many of the saints in prison.
The saints were followers of Jesus.
When the saints were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.
passages.original: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησα ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις καὶ πολλούς τε τῶν ἁγίων ἐγὼ ἐν φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβών ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον

passages.text: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a zealous persecutor of Christians.
He punished Christians often.
He punished them in every synagogue.
He tried to force them to blaspheme.
He was extremely angry with them.
He persecuted them with great fury.
He even traveled to foreign cities to persecute them.
passages.original: καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐτοὺς ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς ἐδίωκον ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις

passages.text: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
I once persecuted Christians.
I received authority from the chief priests.
They gave me permission and orders.
I traveled to Damascus.
I went there to continue my persecution.
passages.original: Ἐν οἷς πορευόμενος εἰς τὴν Δαμασκὸν μετ’ ἐξουσίας καὶ ἐπιτροπῆς τῆς τῶν ἀρχιερέων

passages.text: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.
passages.sermon:
Paul was traveling to Damascus.
Paul had authority from the chief priests.
Paul was persecuting Christians.
Paul spoke to King Agrippa.
It was about noon.
Paul was on the road.
Paul saw a light from heaven.
The light was brighter than the sun.
The light shone around Paul.
The light also shone around Paul's companions.
passages.original: ἡμέρας μέσης κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν εἶδον βασιλεῦ οὐρανόθεν ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου περιλάμψαν με φῶς καὶ τοὺς σὺν ἐμοὶ πορευομένους

passages.text: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
passages.sermon:
Paul was traveling to Damascus.
He had authority and a commission from the chief priests.
He saw a light from heaven at noon.
The light was brighter than the sun.
The light shone around Paul and his companions.
All of them fell to the ground.
Paul heard a voice.
The voice spoke to Paul in Hebrew.
The voice said, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”
The voice also said, “It is hard for you to kick against the goads.”
passages.original: πάντων τε καταπεσόντων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἤκουσα φωνὴν λέγουσαν πρός με τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ τί με διώκεις σκληρόν σοι πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν

passages.text: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.
passages.sermon:
Saul spoke to the voice from heaven.
He asked, "Who are You, Lord?"
The Lord answered Saul.
The Lord said, "I am Jesus."
Jesus said, "You are persecuting Me."
passages.original: Ἐγὼ δὲ εἶπα Τίς εἶ Κύριε Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εἶπεν Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις

passages.text: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Saul.
Jesus told Saul to get up.
Jesus told Saul to stand on his feet.
Jesus said He appeared to Saul for a reason.
Jesus said He chose Saul to be a servant.
Jesus said He chose Saul to be a witness.
Jesus said Saul would witness what he had already seen from Jesus.
Jesus said Saul would also witness what Jesus would show him in the future.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ στῆθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὤφθην σοι προχειρίσασθαί σε ὑπηρέτην καὶ μάρτυρα ὧν τε εἶδές με ὧν τε ὀφθήσομαί σοι

passages.text: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Paul.
Jesus said, “I will rescue you from your own people.
I will also rescue you from the Gentiles.
I am sending you to these people.
You will open their eyes.
They will turn from darkness to light.
They will turn from the power of Satan to God.
They will receive forgiveness of sins.
They will receive a share with those who are made holy by faith in Me.”
passages.original: ἐξαιρούμενός σε ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς οὓς ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω σε ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν τοῦ ἐπιστρέψαι ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς καὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐπὶ τὸν Θεόν τοῦ λαβεῖν αὐτοὺς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ κλῆρον ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πίστει τῇ εἰς ἐμέ

passages.text: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
passages.sermon: Paul spoke to King Agrippa.\r\nPaul said he was not disobedient.\r\nPaul obeyed the vision from heaven.
passages.original: Ὅθεν βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα οὐκ ἐγενόμην ἀπειθὴς τῇ οὐρανίῳ ὀπτασίᾳ

passages.text: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul obeyed the heavenly vision.
Paul spoke first to the people in Damascus.
Paul spoke next to the people in Jerusalem.
Paul spoke to everyone in the region of Judea.
Paul also spoke to the Gentiles.
Paul told them to repent.
Paul told them to turn to God.
Paul told them to do deeds that show true repentance.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐν Δαμασκῷ πρῶτόν τε καὶ Ἱεροσολύμοις πᾶσάν τε τὴν χώραν τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπήγγελλον μετανοεῖν καὶ ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ τὸν Θεόν ἄξια τῆς μετανοίας ἔργα πράσσοντας

passages.text: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
passages.sermon: The Jews saw me in the temple courts.\r\nThey seized me there.\r\nThey tried to kill me because of these things.
passages.original: ἕνεκα τούτων με Ἰουδαῖοι συλλαβόμενοι ὄντα ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐπειρῶντο διαχειρίσασθαι

passages.text: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”
passages.sermon:
God has helped me until today.
I stand here now.
I testify to everyone.
I speak to both important and unimportant people.
I do not say anything new.
I only say what the prophets said would happen.
I only say what Moses said would happen.
The prophets and Moses said the Christ would suffer.
They said the Christ would be the first to rise from the dead.
They said the Christ would bring light to our people.
They said the Christ would bring light to the Gentiles.
passages.original: Ἐπικουρίας οὖν τυχὼν τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἕστηκα μαρτυρόμενος μικρῷ τε καὶ μεγάλῳ οὐδὲν ἐκτὸς λέγων ὧν τε οἱ προφῆται ἐλάλησαν μελλόντων γίνεσθαι καὶ Μωϋσῆς εἰ παθητὸς ὁ Χριστός εἰ πρῶτος ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν φῶς μέλλει καταγγέλλειν τῷ τε λαῷ καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν

passages.text: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”
passages.sermon:
Paul was defending himself before the authorities.
Festus was present during Paul’s defense.
Festus spoke with a loud voice.
Festus said, “Paul, you are insane!”
Festus said, “Your great learning is driving you to madness!”
passages.original: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπολογουμένου ὁ Φῆστος μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ φησιν Μαίνῃ Παῦλε τὰ πολλά σε γράμματα εἰς μανίαν περιτρέπει

passages.text: But Paul answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before Festus, the Roman governor.
Festus had just accused Paul of being insane.
Paul replied to Festus.
Paul said, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus.
I speak words of truth.
I speak words of sound judgment.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος Οὐ μαίνομαι φησίν Κράτιστε Φῆστε ἀλλὰ ἀληθείας καὶ σωφροσύνης ῥήματα ἀποφθέγγομαι

passages.text: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.
passages.sermon:
King Agrippa knows about these matters.
I can speak openly to him.
Nothing about these events has escaped his notice.
I am sure of this.
These things did not happen in secret.
Everyone could see them.
passages.original: ἐπίσταται γὰρ περὶ τούτων ὁ βασιλεύς πρὸς ὃν καὶ παρρησιαζόμενος λαλῶ λανθάνειν γὰρ αὐτὸν τι τούτων οὐ πείθομαι οὐθέν οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἐν γωνίᾳ πεπραγμένον τοῦτο

passages.text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before King Agrippa.
Paul spoke directly to King Agrippa.
Paul asked King Agrippa a question.
Paul said, “King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets?”
Paul answered his own question.
Paul said, “I know that you believe.”
passages.original: πιστεύεις βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα τοῖς προφήταις οἶδα ὅτι πιστεύεις

passages.text: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”
passages.sermon:
King Agrippa spoke to Paul.
Agrippa asked Paul a question.
Agrippa said, “You are trying to persuade me.”
Agrippa said, “You are trying to persuade me in a short time.”
Agrippa said, “You want me to become a Christian quickly.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἀγρίππας πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον Ἐν ὀλίγῳ με πείθεις Χριστιανὸν ποιῆσαι

passages.text: “Short time or long,” Paul replied, “I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian.
Paul was a prisoner.
Paul spoke to King Agrippa and others who listened.
Paul replied to King Agrippa.
Paul said, “I pray to God for you.”
Paul said, “I pray for everyone who hears me today.”
Paul wanted them to become like him.
Paul wanted them to be Christians.
Paul did not want them to be prisoners.
Paul said, “I want you to be as I am, except for these chains.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος Εὐξαίμην ἂν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ καὶ ἐν μεγάλῳ οὐ μόνον σὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντάς μου σήμερον γενέσθαι τοιούτους ὁποῖος καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι παρεκτὸς τῶν δεσμῶν τούτων

passages.text: Then the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.
passages.sermon:
The king stood up.
The governor stood up.
Bernice stood up.
The people sitting with them stood up.
passages.original: Ἀνέστη τε ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἥ τε Βερνίκη καὶ οἱ συνκαθήμενοι αὐτοῖς

passages.text: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”
passages.sermon:
The people left the room.
They spoke to each other.
They talked about Paul.
They said Paul had done nothing wrong.
They said Paul did nothing that deserved death.
They said Paul did nothing that deserved prison.
passages.original: καὶ ἀναχωρήσαντες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες ὅτι Οὐδὲν θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἄξιον τι πράσσει ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος

passages.text: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
passages.sermon:
King Agrippa spoke to Festus.
Agrippa said something about Paul.
Paul was the man on trial.
Agrippa said Paul could have been set free.
Paul had appealed to Caesar.
Because Paul appealed to Caesar, they could not release him.
passages.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ τῷ Φήστῳ ἔφη Ἀπολελύσθαι ἐδύνατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰ μὴ ἐπεκέκλητο Καίσαρα
